messages.text: Is the power kit and the miner kit are important to buy ?
Read the harlo h15 dual page
Searched the catalog · power kit miner kit accessory

Short answer: neither is required. The H15 ships with its power cord and the PSU built in, so it runs out of the box.

The P. Kit ($69.99) is an energy cost monitor. Handy on day one if you want a real number for what the miner costs to run at your rate, rather than a spec sheet figure.

The Miner Duster ($39.99) is the maintenance one, dust is what slowly kills a home miner.

Which did you mean by "miner kit", the Duster?
Thank you
Happy to help. One thing I'm curious about, since you're looking at the H15 Dual: is the Dogecoin side what drew you to it, or were you mainly after the Bitcoin hashrate?
Is it easy to install

Yes, it's a plug-and-play unit. Power supply is built in, so it's the cord into the wall, then either ethernet or WiFi, and you set your pool and wallet in the web dashboard from a browser. Most people are hashing in about ten minutes.

Two honest notes: the WiFi is 2.4 GHz only, so if your router hides that band you'll want the ethernet cable. And at ~50 dB and ~500W it's not a bedroom machine.

The H15 Dual is $999 and ships November 14, 2026. Want the link?
Ethernit is better ?

Yes, if you can run a cable, use ethernet. A miner holds a connection 24/7 and a dropped WiFi link means lost shares until it reconnects. Ethernet just never does that.

WiFi works fine too, plenty of people run it that way. Keep the unit within good signal of the router and on the 2.4 GHz band.

Is there an outlet near your router, or would it be sitting somewhere else in the house?
One more stupid question, how much make aday , whats the estimate
Ran the power-cost calculator

Not a stupid question, it's the right one.

Honest version: at home retail power, a 15 TH/s unit is about stacking sats slowly plus a solo-block lottery ticket, not daily profit. At ~500W it runs roughly 12 kWh a day, so your electricity rate decides most of it.

Tell me your state or country and I'll run the real numbers for you, sats a month, power cost and the break-even BTC price, so you can judge it before you spend $999.
Massachusetts
Ran the power-cost calculator

Massachusetts is one of the pricier states for electricity, so that matters here. The H15 at ~500W runs about 12 kWh a day, and whatever your rate per kWh is, multiply by 12 for your daily cost. Your bill will show the rate.

If pure Bitcoin per dollar is the goal, the Magic Miner 40T ($799, 40 TH/s, ships November 14, 2026) gives you more hashrate for less money than the H15. The H15's real draw is mining Dogecoin and Litecoin at the same time.

Which matters more to you?
How long they will take me to get my money back ?

Straight answer: at Massachusetts electricity prices, I wouldn't buy one expecting it to pay itself back. Home mining at retail power is about stacking sats steadily, plus a real but long-odds shot at a solo block, and the upside comes mostly from Bitcoin's price later, not from daily earnings now.

Anyone promising you a payback date is guessing, because BTC price and network difficulty both move.

If that framing doesn't appeal, honestly, don't buy. If it does, the question is just which unit.
Thank you so much

Any time. Take your time deciding, the H15 Dual and the Magic Miner 40T both show Ships November 14, 2026, so there's no rush today.

If you want help picking later, or a hand at setup once it lands, come back here or join our Discord, plenty of home miners in there: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

And if you found this useful, a word on Trustpilot would mean a lot to us: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/heliumdeploy.com
Wich one is good for me

If it's your first miner and Massachusetts power is what it is, I'd start small: the Hammer Miner BC04, 6 TH/s at about 100W, $239, in stock and ships in a few days. Low cost to find out whether you enjoy it.

If you're already sure and want the most Bitcoin per dollar, the Magic Miner 40T, $799 for 40 TH/s, ships November 14, 2026.

The H15 Dual only wins if Dogecoin and Litecoin matter to you.

Want a link to the BC04?
Ok

Here it is, the Hammer Miner BC04, 6 TH/s, $239: https://heliumdeploy.com/products/hammer-miner-bc04

The plug is matched to your shipping address, so there's nothing to pick. It's in stock and ships from our US warehouse within about 5 business days, and no import tax applies inside the US.

Want me to build the cart so you can go straight to checkout?
I do have a helium miner

Good to know, that's a different animal though. A Helium hotspot earns from coverage and sips a few watts; a Bitcoin ASIC earns from hashrate and eats 100W and up. So the Helium rewards don't really carry over.

If you liked the set-and-forget side of Helium, we also carry Wingbits (ADS-B) and a WeatherXM station, same idea, low power, passive earning.

Which appeals more, more DePIN like that, or actually mining Bitcoin?
Whats wingbits
Searched the catalog · Wingbits

Wingbits is aircraft tracking. The device picks up ADS-B signals from planes overhead and feeds that data to the network, and you earn points now, with $WINGS tokens planned later. Low power, no noise, set and forget, much closer to your Helium hotspot than an ASIC is.

The catch: it has to go outdoors with a clear view of the sky, so a roof or a mast. Line of sight is everything.

The W.200 is $475, in stock: https://heliumdeploy.com/products/wingbits-wb200

Do you have a roof spot for it?
Ido have

Then it's a good fit for you. Weatherproof, runs on ethernet or WiFi, and it reaches planes up to 250 nautical miles out.

One honest note: rewards depend on how well covered your area already is. Dense spots near Boston have more receivers competing; a quieter area is usually worth more to the network.

The W.200 is $475, in stock, ships from our US warehouse in about 5 business days.

Want me to build the cart so you can check out?
Please and thank you
